text:
talia-people: Quick one from Ben's team: Casey is on intermittent parental leave starting Nov 15 and plans to be out intermittently through Jan. Their regular PTO year ends Dec 31 and the blackout is Dec 20-31. Manager asked if unused PTO during leave can carry into next year or be advanced to cover planned days in Jan.

mike-peopleops-sr: Short take: employees accrue PTO while active; during unpaid parental leave accrual rules vary by leave type. Continuous paid parental leave accrues per policy; intermittent leave may not. We'll need to know if Casey is on paid company parental leave or unpaid FMLA-style leave.

emma-people: Added detail: If Casey is on Redwood-paid parental leave then PTO does not get consumed for the paid weeks. If they're using intermittent unpaid leave, PTO is used unless an accommodation is requested. For carryover: standard employee carryover policy applies; exceptions across year-end require People Ops + Manager sign-off and Finance approval if accrual impacts books.

ben-engineering: Manager here. Casey expects to be back intermittently for a few days in Dec and more in Jan. Team is stretched during blackout so manager wants to pre-approve advancing 3 PTO days into Jan (so Casey can be paid for those Jan days without waiting for future accrual). Is that allowed?

ginger-benefits: We can advance PTO (negative balance) as a one-time exception for employees with a strong return-to-work plan, but it must be documented and is only for employees (not contractors). Payroll needs an accrual adjustment entry and a signed manager/employee agreement. Example CSV for payroll: 

worker_id, action, days, note
77123, ADVANCE_PTO, 3, "Advance for Jan coverage during parental leave; signed agreement on file"

Send to payroll@redwood.com and cc people-ops. Finance will review if this changes year-end liabilities.

mike-peopleops-sr: Important: because this touches the year-end blackout (2026-12-20 to 2026-12-31), approvals must be in writing before blackout. Also document contingency coverage in the team rota. If Finance declines the advance because of accounting close, fallback is to allow unpaid days or comp-days (if team covers).

ben-engineering: OK. Which is fastest: (A) sign agreement + payroll CSV, or (B) request comp-days from teammates to cover Jan days? Teammates are willing to swap shifts.

ginger-benefits: Fastest to get Casey paid = APPROVE advance + payroll CSV (if Finance signs off quickly). Fastest to get coverage without payroll = comp-day swap (manager documents who covers which dates and payroll logs comp-days). For comp-days we accept: 

worker_id, reason, comp_date, pay_code
77123, "comp for coverage swap", 2027-01-06, COMP-DAY

Also include coverer worker_id and note in your message.

calendar-bot: Reminder: Year-end blackout 2026-12-20 to 2026-12-31. Any exceptions require Manager + People Ops sign-off and must be recorded.

mike-peopleops-sr: Next steps: Ben, please (1) confirm whether Casey is on paid parental leave or unpaid intermittent leave, (2) get Casey+manager to sign the advance agreement if you choose advance, OR (3) confirm comp-day coverers and have them confirm in thread. I'll queue Finance review once you reply.

ben-engineering: I'll confirm leave type and loop Casey in now. Team can likely cover two days as comp-swaps; manager and Casey prefer advance for 3 days if Finance OK. Will update this thread shortly.

talia-people: Thanks — I'll prep a simple advance agreement template and attach it to the People Ops ticket when you confirm. Ticket will include liability estimate for Finance. :thumbsup:
